name: Fraud-Detection-System
description: Fraud classifier on 6.3M simulated PaySim mobile-money transactions. XGBoost with a time-based split: 99.9% precision and 99.6% recall on a 132K-row holdout (99.98% of fraud value stopped, 3 false alarms), walk-forward PR-AUC 0.997, live scoring demo.

paragraphs: A model that flags fraudulent mobile-money transfers so they can be stopped before the money leaves. On 132,136 transactions it had never seen, it stopped 99.98% of the fraud value (the simulator's built-in flag stopped 1.1%), catching 2,742 of 2,754 frauds while wrongly flagging 3 legitimate ones. XGBoost trained on 6.3 million simulated PaySim transactions, with a live scoring demo.
Try it: live scoring page · dashboard (free host, allow about 30 seconds to wake)

In mobile money a fraud flag usually freezes the customer's funds. Every false alarm locks an honest customer out of their own money; every missed fraud is a direct loss. Fraud is about 0.13% of transactions, so a model that never flags anything is 99.87% accurate and useless. A fraud-operations team needs three answers from a model: how much fraud value it stops, how many honest customers it freezes to do so, and whether that holds up as time passes. This page answers them in that order.
